title: Support ticket
blurb: One message, three kinds of question.
lesson: One state can answer many questions at once. The Choice names a team with a probability for each option, the Noul gives the probability of yes, and the Score places the customer's mood on a scale.

title: Spam and scam check
blurb: Yes or no questions about a suspicious message.
lesson: A Noul answers with the probability of yes, not a hard decision. Read how close each answer is to the ends before you trust it, and compare the questions: two questions about the same message can get very different answers.

title: Review rating
blurb: A star Score and the main complaint.
lesson: A Score reads a position on your scale. The probabilities across the levels show how torn Jev is, and a low confidence on the Choice is a sign the review mixes several complaints.

title: Resume fit
blurb: Match a candidate to a role.
lesson: Jev screens a short profile quickly, but a fit question is a judgment call. Treat the probabilities as a first pass for a person to review, never as the final decision about a candidate.

title: Post moderation
blurb: Private details, tone and what to do.
lesson: Jev is strong at flagging a post for review. When the Choice about what to do has a low confidence, the case is a real judgment call, and that is the point to hand it to a person.

title: Counting trap
blurb: Questions that ask Jev to count.
lesson: Counting is a known weak spot of System One models. Jev may get a list right, but you can never be sure, so use plain code when you need an exact count. The Sandbox warns you when a question asks to count.
